name: Telheiras / Lumiar
summary: A neighbourhood solar community promoted by Viver Telheiras and the Lumiar parish council, with vulnerable households included.
evidence: The organiser reports two production units and 70 members on its community page. This is an organiser report, not an independent outcome audit.
lesson: Build participation and advice around a local organisation people already know.
unknowns: Audited savings, current joining availability and registration documents have not been verified.

name: Agra do Amial
summary: A solar energy community involving municipal housing and a local school, developed through Asprela + Sustentável.
evidence: The municipality describes the community as an ERSE pilot. Porto’s 2024 sustainability report says it began operating in May 2024.
lesson: Municipal buildings and housing can anchor a community with a social purpose.
unknowns: Current membership, independently measured savings and open participation have not been verified.

name: Coopérnico
summary: A Portuguese renewable-energy cooperative with citizen investment, electricity supply and community-development support.
evidence: Its website documents membership, supply and renewable-generation investment. A nationwide cooperative is a different model from a single local sharing group.
lesson: Cooperative ownership can connect member capital to renewable generation.
unknowns: Legal CER/CCE classification of individual projects must be checked separately. Member benefits depend on the service or project.

name: SANJOTEC
summary: A technology-park solar community with Cleanwatts, combining rooftop panels and parking canopies with local energy sharing.
evidence: SANJOTEC’s 15 August 2026 announcement reports operation and the installed capacity. The annual production and own-use split (see the case study below) are organiser estimates.
lesson: A host site with daytime consumption can anchor sharing with nearby participants.
unknowns: Measured yearly production, realised savings, legal registration and current joining availability require confirmation.

name: Autódromo Internacional do Algarve
summary: A large rooftop solar project at the Algarve motorsport complex, presented by SES Energia as an energy community.
evidence: SES’s 27 August 2025 case study reports more than 1,151 kWp and local sharing. This differs from the research report’s approximate 1 MW figure.
lesson: A substantial host can anchor generation, but local participation and governance still need evidence.
unknowns: Independent operating data, member governance, registration and realised savings have not been established.

name: Adega Cultural de Vila Verde
summary: A rural photovoltaic energy-sharing pilot at a municipal cultural venue, documented by CIM Cávado.
evidence: The intermunicipal authority says the pilot is already functioning and describes generation, consumption and sharing.
lesson: Local public institutions can provide a site and coordination for a rural demonstration.
unknowns: Capacity, measured outcomes, legal registration and current membership are undisclosed in the reviewed page.

name: Miranda do Douro
summary: A community project associated with the local Santa Casa da Misericórdia and Cleanwatts.
evidence: Cleanwatts reports establishing a community in August 2021 and identifies the Santa Casa in its organisation history.
lesson: Social institutions can host generation and help connect a project to local needs.
unknowns: Present operational status, capacity, energy output, member numbers and formal registration have not been independently verified.

name: Som Energia
summary: A member-based renewable-energy cooperative combining electricity supply and generation projects.
evidence: The cooperative publishes its supply, production and participation model. Included as a European example, without asserting Portuguese eligibility.
lesson: Look at member participation and governance alongside the technical system.
unknowns: Eligibility and availability vary by local project. This entry does not establish REC/CEC status under a particular national scheme.

name: Ecopower
summary: A citizen-owned cooperative investing in renewable generation and supplying electricity to its members.
evidence: The organisation describes cooperative ownership of wind, solar, batteries and heat networks. This is organisation-reported activity.
lesson: Long-term ownership and supply can reinforce one another within a cooperative.
unknowns: This is not a local Portuguese ACC template. Current membership conditions and project-level outcomes require direct review.
